title: Annulus fibrosus
summary: Quasi-static tensile stress-strain curves of human annulus: single lamella along fibres, uniaxial circumferential and axial, and biaxial with circumferential strain held.
simulate: Build each specimen as stated: single lamella strip (fibres along the load), multi-lamella strip, cruciform, or square; lamellae at about +-30 deg to the transverse (circumferential) direction.
Orient the load: along fibres (lamella), circumferential, or axial; biaxial = axial stretch with the circumferential grips (or strain) held.
Grip the ends (bony ends rigid); leave lateral faces free except in biaxial; start from the load-free state after any stated preload.
Load quasi-statically (experiments: 0.0001 /s or slower, 1 mm/min, or equilibrium after stepwise holds) up to the last strain of each curve.
Report nominal stress (force / undeformed cross-section, MPa) against nominal strain (%) as one curve per simulation, from a central gauge region where the study used one.

studies.sample: 11 lumbar discs, grade I-II; curves = 4 single lamellae (VLe, VLi, De, Di) of one representative unit
studies.loading: Displacement control, tension along fibres at 1 mm/min to >1 MPa (to ~20% strain); load-free start; 5 preconditioning cycles; 37 °C; single AF lamellae

studies.sample: 59 single-lamella dumbbells, 13 L2-L3 discs, grade I-II (AO, AI, PO, PI); curve = cubic fit of one typical specimen
studies.loading: Uniaxial tension along fibres at 0.00009/s to failure (~5.6%); 0.1 N tare 15 min; 10 precond. cycles to 0.05 N; 0.15 M NaCl, room temp; single lamellae

studies.sample: 11 circumferential anterior AF strips, grade I-II, 6 spines; curve evaluated from mean fit coefficients
studies.loading: Uniaxial circumferential tension at 0.0001/s to 0.4 MPa (~8% strain); no tare load; 10 preconditioning cycles; saline bath; anterior full-depth AF strips

studies.sample: 60 anterior AF strips, 10 non-degenerate L1-L3 discs; curves = one representative disc (equilibrium)
studies.loading: Stepwise stress relaxation (1-4% steps, 15 min each) to 20% circ / 40% axial strain; 0.008 MPa tare; 10 preconditioning cycles; anterior AF strips

studies.sample: 5 outer anterior AF cruciform specimens, grade I-II; curves = one typical specimen
studies.loading: Displacement control, axial stretch at <0.0001/s (circ. free or held) to ~8% circ / ~25% axial strain; 0.5 N preload; 3 precond. cycles; outer anterior AF

studies.sample: outer anterior AF strips, L3-L5; 7 non-degenerate (curves = one representative sample)
studies.loading: Displacement control, quasi-static uniaxial ramp to ~16-18% strain (circ, axial); 0.1 N preload 10 min; 20 precond. cycles to 2%; outer anterior AF strips

studies.sample: Bass 2004 typical specimen, E22=0 biaxial run, digitised from Ghezelbash 2021 Fig 5b,c
studies.loading: Displacement control, biaxial: axial stretch at <0.0001/s to ~11% with circ. strain held at 0; 0.5 N preload; outer anterior AF cruciform (per review)

studies.sample: 16 anterior AF circ-axial squares (7.1x7.0x2.1 mm), L3-L5, 13 spines 25-80 y, T1rho 46-146 ms; curve = Fig 3b circ-fixed run
studies.loading: Biaxial, axial stretch at 0.01%/s with circ. strain held at 0, to E~0.09 (cap 1.5 MPa); 0.5 N preload 10 min; 10 precond. cycles 0-2% at 1%/s; PBS, room temp; anterior AF squares

studies.sample: 60 circumferential multi-layer AF strips (AO, AI, PO, PI; 15 each), L3-L4, 15 spines 26-53 y, grade I-II; curves = one typical grade I disc (28 y)
studies.loading: Displacement control, circ. tension at 0.07 mm/min (~0.0001/s) to failure (~15%); 0.1 N tare 15 min; 10 precond. cycles; L3-L4 AF strips (AO, AI, PO, PI)

views.title: Annulus stress–strain, per test mode
views.note: Nominal stress vs nominal strain (stretch − 1) of the central region. Single lamella: fibres on the load axis. Strips: fibres about ±30° (circumferential) or ±60° (axial) to the load, sides free. Biaxial: circumferential direction held.

notes: Definitions follow Ghezelbash et al. 2021 (Acta Biomater submission, SSRN 3677348, Fig 4 caption, p.20): nominal strain = applied displacement / initial length; nominal stress = applied force / initial cross-sectional area (first Piola-Kirchhoff); Ghezelbash et al. 2020 (J Biomech 102:109463, Fig 2, p.4) plots 'Nominal Stress' vs 'Engineering Strain'.

Test modes are those the two papers validated against (2020 Sec 2.2 p.2, Fig 2; 2021 Figs 4, 5, 7): single lamella along fibres, uniaxial circumferential and axial, biaxial. Shear, radial, bone-AF-bone failure, rate, creep/relaxation-time and fatigue data are left out.

Most curves are one representative specimen (n=1); Wagner & Lotz is a mean-coefficient fit (derived). Lagrangian strains E (Bass, O'Connell) were converted to nominal strain as sqrt(1+2E) - 1; stresses are as reported. Elliott & Setton values are equilibrium (end of stepwise holds).
agent_prompt: You are given a constitutive or finite element model of human lumbar annulus fibrosus. Run the 4 simulations in `simulations`, one per test mode: single lamella along the fibres, uniaxial circumferential, uniaxial axial, and biaxial (axial stretch with the circumferential direction held). Load quasi-statically and report nominal stress (force / undeformed cross-section, MPa) against nominal strain (change in length / initial length, %); for biaxial also transverse_stress = the circumferential (held-direction) nominal stress. Each curve is compared with the range spanned by all studies, regions and specimens of that mode. Use one parameter set for all simulations. Run each simulation once, sweeping the input in `sweep` over all its listed values (start from the unloaded state; a denser curve is fine), and record every listed output. Return one JSON object following answer_format: per simulation id, one curve [[x, y], ...] per output (x = the sweep input; it is read by linear interpolation and listed x values outside your curve fail), or one number where there is no sweep or the output is marked scalar; null where your model cannot run it. Do not tune the model to the reference values.
